text: The majority of private fund advisers in the United States are not considering changing their assets under management in order to lower Dodd-Frank compliance costs, notwithstanding the $150 million registration threshold and the $1.5 billion Form PF quarterly reporting threshold.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study (2016). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=2732915

isBasedOn.name: The Private Fund Industry Five Years after the Dodd-Frank Act – A Survey Study

abstract: the majority response to Survey Question 7 implies that the majority of private fund advisers in the United States are not considering changing their AUM in order to lower their Dodd-Frank Act compliance costs.
